oewn-10480990-n.learner: a person or thing that has or uses power, influence or authority
examples: She felt that some evil power was at work in the old house.
He hit the ball with all the power in his arms.

oewn-11470903-n.learner: energy you get when electricity flows through a wire or other material that carries it
examples: The power went out during the storm, and the house went dark.

oewn-08194510-n.learner: a country strong enough to change what happens all over the world
examples: After the war the country grew into a world power.

oewn-11473433-n.learner: in physics, how fast work is done, measured in watts (joules each second)
examples: The motor has a power of 500 watts.

oewn-06825275-n.learner: a small number written in maths to show how many times a number is multiplied by itself
examples: Two to the power of three is eight.

oewn-09859605-n.learner: a very rich or powerful person in business
examples: He was a power in the steel business, rich enough to buy the whole town.

oewn-07465938-n.learner: formal ceremony held for important occasions
examples: The new queen was crowned with great pomp and circumstance.

oewn-02344882-s.learner: too little to give what is needed
examples: Money was short that winter, so the family ate less meat.

oewn-00643682-s.learner: saying very little in a way that is rude, or that sounds like an order no one may question
examples: When he asked a third time, she was short with him.

connotation.why: calls a brief manner rude where 'brief' would not

oewn-02345399-s.learner: less than the right, legal, or full amount, often on purpose.
examples: The baker was fined for selling bread of short weight.

oewn-01902113-s.learner: not thinking far enough ahead, or not taking in enough of the problem
examples: Selling the farm to pay one bill was a short view of their troubles.

connotation.why: faults the thinking as lacking foresight

oewn-02013127-a.learner: used of memory: not good at keeping things, or not reaching very far
examples: Voters have short memories, and the scandal was soon forgotten.

oewn-01447121-a.learner: used of speech sounds or syllables: taking less time to say than others
examples: The 'a' in 'cat' is a short vowel.

oewn-01447511-a.learner: not owning the shares or goods you are selling, because you expect their price to fall
examples: Traders who were short in oil made money when the price fell.

oewn-00712466-s.learner: tending to crumble or break into flakes because it is made with a lot of fat
examples: Her pastry was short and melted in the mouth.
He sent a minute to the manager about the broken lift.

oewn-05138288-n.learner: how far away something is, counted by how long it takes to get there
examples: The station is ten minutes from here on foot.

oewn-13632810-n.learner: a unit for measuring angles, equal to one sixtieth of a degree
examples: The ship's position was given to the nearest minute of latitude.

oewn-00595453-v.learner: to feel for someone and accept their feelings or reasons
examples: Don't worry about missing the party; I understand.

oewn-00595247-v.learner: to know what the words of a language mean
examples: She understands French but cannot speak it.

oewn-10391440-n.learner: a person given the right to hold a position of authority on a ship
examples: The ship's first officer took the wheel while the captain slept.

oewn-02555278-v.learner: to take care of something or deal with it
examples: I have some business to attend to before lunch.

oewn-02546367-v.learner: to work for someone, or to be their servant
examples: Two maids attended the old lady day and night.

oewn-07560785-n.learner: a feeling of friendship together with a high opinion of someone
examples: Over the years the two old rivals came to feel a warm respect for each other.

oewn-14461018-n.learner: the state of being honoured or thought well of
examples: The old doctor was held in great respect in the village.

oewn-01135185-n.learner: behaviour meant to please your parents
examples: The boy kept every rule at home out of respect for his parents.

oewn-00081834-v.learner: to make the condition of someone or something better
examples: Fresh air and sleep helped the sick boy more than any medicine.

oewn-02561142-v.learner: to add to the progress of something
examples: The new road helped the growth of trade in the town.

oewn-00207406-v.learner: to make something better; to change it for the better
examples: A new rug will really help this dull room.

oewn-01183592-v.learner: to serve someone some food, or give them food or drink
examples: May I help you to some more potatoes?

oewn-01196102-v.learner: to take something or make use of it
examples: Help yourself to a pen from the box on my desk.
It is no matter if you are late; we will wait.

oewn-00021007-n.learner: anything that has mass and takes up space
examples: Everything around us, from air to stone, is made of matter.

oewn-06376912-n.learner: written works, especially in books or magazines
examples: She packed plenty of reading matter for the long train journey.
